top_rigor_problems: Invented attribution: F4-T puts born-again-from-above teaching in Origen's Commentary on John, whose surviving books do not reach John 3; the records give regeneration to Clement.

Stratum and place slippage: Gregory's Caesarea account is used as 'our student'/an Alexandrian day (F1-P, F5-I, F5-P) against alx.quote.gregory-spark's not_for, and F5-I invents a routine and asserts the non-literate majority's inner life.

Unhedged single-source claims: 'Origen learned from Clement' (C-E) and 'our meeting places were known' (F3-E) have no record behind them; F6-T closes by generalizing Origen's remedial view to 'we held'.
top_access_problems: Engine cuts leave orphan references: C-P 'It was love... for the man who taught him', F5-E 'that is a word to the wealthy', F6-P 'The kindling was not forced'.
Overlong self-audit: F2-E (836 words) talks about the build ('honest service to the participant') instead of answering.

Recycled blocks and padding: dw text pasted where off-topic (God-as-teacher in C-T, failures paragraph in F6-E, F6-I repeats F3-P, long death quote in F6-T); chatbot openers ('That is the center.', 'The first ask is').
world_summary.cost_note: Output tokens concentrate in F2-E (1229 out, ~550 words beyond need), F4-I (794), F5-P (681), F5-I (604), F2-P (587) and F6-T (447 out but ~180 words off-question). Capping answers near 260 words and stopping reuse of whole dw paragraphs would cut roughly 2,000 surplus words across the set with no loss of substance.
world_summary.go_live_view: Close to fit. 20 of 28 ship as is; the doctrine, authority, failure and limits answers are accurate, well hedged and in a plain, humane voice, and the honest limits (material remains, marriage, women's words) are spoken well. Two answers must be blocked (F4-T invented Origen attribution; F5-I invented daily routine and claims about the majority) and six need craft fixes, mostly orphan references from cut sentences and padding. The single most valuable fix is in the engine: when a sentence or quote is cut (Gregory spark, Clement couches), also drop the sentences that point back to it, and forbid attributing a teaching to a named author/work unless a cited record carries that attribution.
